questions.q: Which four families of measure does the lesson use to frame service analytics?
options: Leads, opportunities, quotes, orders
Volume, backlog, speed and customer impact
Revenue, cost, margin and tax
Campaigns, members, responses and ROI
questions.explain: Service questions map to volume, backlog, speed and customer impact, all measured from the Case object.

questions.q: How do you find which customers open the most cases?
options: Group a case report by Account Name and summarize Record Count
Group an opportunity report by Stage
Sort a lead report by Created Date
Use a cross filter on Campaigns
questions.explain: Grouping cases by account gives the customer lens. Add priority or escalation filters to find customers under strain.

questions.q: A leader asks for SLA compliance on cases. What must exist first?
options: Nothing, it is a standard column on every case
A dashboard filter
A joined report
Data captured through Entitlements and Milestones or custom timestamps
questions.explain: SLA and response-time measures depend on admin-configured entitlement processes or custom date fields; without them there is nothing to report.

questions.q: Why should you state whether a report counts cases opened or cases closed in the period?
options: Because Salesforce only supports one of them
Because the two give different numbers and answer different questions
Because closed cases are deleted
Because it changes the object being reported on
questions.explain: Cases opened measures demand; cases closed measures throughput. Mixing them up causes confusing comparisons.

questions.q: Where do customer satisfaction scores usually come from in a native Salesforce report?
options: They are automatically calculated from case age
They are always in the Contact standard fields
Surveys, either through survey features in some editions, a custom field, or another system
They are derived from the Priority field
questions.explain: CSAT is not inferred from case data. It has to be captured through a survey process and stored somewhere reportable.
